headline: US markets took a hammering last night with the NASDAQ down 5.3%, while the ASX held steady today — and GTA VI just had the biggest entertainment launch in history.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS bounced strongly today, up 4.6% to $2.74. Traders are betting on low Chinese lithium stockpiles eventually forcing buyers back to the market, giving beaten-down miners a short-term lift. The stock is still deeply underwater long-term, but this is a rare green day for lithium bulls.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dropped 2.8% last night in a broad tech selloff that hammered the NASDAQ. There was no Microsoft-specific bad news — the whole sector sold off hard, likely on renewed concerns about stretched valuations and macro pressures. The long-term AI growth story remains intact.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google fell 2.6% last night as part of the same wide tech rout that hit the NASDAQ. No Google-specific catalyst — this was sector-wide pain. The long-term case for Google's AI and search dominance hasn't changed.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped 1.6% today on the ASX, tracking the brutal overnight selloff in US tech stocks. As an AI-focused ETF, it's naturally sensitive to moves in US tech giants like those that fell sharply last night on NASDAQ.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO edged up 0.65% last night — a remarkable hold given the NASDAQ was down over 5%. GTA VI reportedly generated $3.79 billion on its first day of release, which is an almost incomprehensible number. That tailwind is clearly keeping buyers interested even in a rough market.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE had a good day on the ASX, up 0.9% to $86.64. Emerging markets can sometimes benefit when US tech sells off hard, as money rotates elsewhere. A quiet positive in an otherwise choppy session.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS slipped 0.6% today. As a US total market ETF, it reflects the overnight NASDAQ carnage — the ASX-listed price is tracking the damage done on Wall Street last night, though the fall was cushioned compared to the raw NASDAQ move.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased 0.3% today — a mild dip given the global tech turbulence. Its diversification across asset classes and geographies is doing exactly what it's supposed to: smoothing out the bumps.

movers.name: DHHF
movers.note: DHHF barely moved today, down just 0.17%. As a broad global ETF, it's well insulated from single-sector swings. Nothing to worry about here — this is normal daily noise.

watch_today.title: NASDAQ crashed 5.3% last night — big hit to US tech holdings
watch_today.detail: The NASDAQ fell 5.28% and the S&P 500 dropped 3.7% last night. That's a serious one-night move, not normal volatility. Your MSFT and GOOG holdings both took ~2.6-2.8% hits, and GXAI.AX followed suit today. But for a long-term buy-and-hold investor, one bad night doesn't change the thesis — sit tight unless something structural has broken (it hasn't).

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA VI launch is a monster catalyst
watch_today.detail: GTA VI reportedly generated $3.79 billion on day one — beating the Nintendo 64's lifetime sales in a single day. This is exactly the event TTWO investors have been waiting years for. The stock held up well last night (+0.65%) even as NASDAQ cratered. Long-term, this is a major validation of the investment thesis. Hold firmly.

watch_today.title: MSFT — solid long-term hold despite last night's dip
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 2.77% last night as part of the broader tech selloff, not due to any company-specific news. The stock is still up 9.35% on your cost base. Microsoft's AI integration across its products (Copilot, Azure, Office) remains one of the strongest long-term stories in tech. This dip doesn't change that.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — a rare green day, but still deeply underwater
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped 4.6% today on optimism around low Chinese lithium stockpiles — the idea being that Chinese battery makers will eventually need to restock and prices will recover. Good news for a beaten-up stock, but PLS is still down nearly 60% on your total investment. The turnaround thesis requires patience. Hold and watch lithium price data.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — underwater and sensitive to US tech swings
watch_today.detail: GXAI is down 22.8% on your cost base and fell another 1.55% today tracking the NASDAQ carnage. AI stocks are volatile and can swing hard on macro sentiment. The long-term AI growth story is real, but this ETF will stay bumpy. No reason to sell — the thesis is intact — but expect more volatility if US tech remains under pressure.

watch_today.title: Treasurer warns of tough year ahead — watch for RBA implications
watch_today.detail: Treasurer Jim Chalmers warned today that unemployment will surpass 5% and inflation forecasts have worsened, calling it an 'economic triple-whammy.' One indicator suggests Australia could tip into recession as early as next month. This matters for your portfolio because a weaker economy could delay RBA rate cuts — keeping pressure on mortgage holders and consumer-facing stocks.

world.summary: The Middle East remains tense with a tanker incident in the Gulf, the UN climate talks collapsed without a major deal, Iran flexed military muscle, and Carlos Alcaraz made tennis history winning the ATP Finals.

stories.title: UN Climate Talks Collapse Without Major Deal
stories.why_it_matters: The latest round of UN climate negotiations broke down without a significant agreement, the second major failure in recent years after COP28. Countries couldn't agree on who should pay for the energy transition in developing nations, with wealthy nations offering far less than the hundreds of billions being demanded. For everyday Australians, this matters because without global action, extreme weather events — floods, heatwaves, bushfires — will keep getting worse and more frequent. It also signals continued uncertainty for clean energy investment globally.

stories.title: Iran Unveils Missile Launcher and Flaunts Military Capabilities
stories.why_it_matters: Iran publicly unveiled a new missile launcher system, with military commanders talking up their capabilities in what they described as an ongoing confrontation with the United States. This comes at the same time as a reported tanker incident in the Gulf of Oman, where Iran claimed two ships caught fire. Middle East tensions directly affect global oil prices — if the Gulf shipping lanes get disrupted, oil spikes fast. Worth watching given oil is already a bit soft at $82.89 a barrel.

stories.title: Tanker Incident Reported in Gulf as Middle East Tensions Simmer
stories.why_it_matters: A tanker incident has been reported in the Gulf as Iran claims two ships caught fire. Details are still developing, but any interference with oil tankers in the Persian Gulf is a serious escalation risk — roughly 20% of the world's oil passes through this region. Combined with Iran's missile displays, the region is in a heightened state of tension. Oil prices and broader market risk sentiment could be affected if this escalates further.

stories.title: West Bank Arson Attacks Condemned as 'Jewish Terrorism' — Israeli Political Feud Erupts
stories.why_it_matters: Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot — a former general and senior political figure — publicly condemned a wave of arson attacks on Palestinian property in the West Bank, calling it 'Jewish terrorism.' Far-right minister Itamar Ben Gvir fired back at him, exposing a deep split within Israel's political establishment over settler violence. This kind of internal Israeli political fracture is rare and significant, suggesting growing pressure on the Netanyahu government from multiple directions simultaneously.

stories.title: Carlos Alcaraz Wins ATP Finals, Joins Exclusive Grand Slam Club
stories.why_it_matters: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alexander Zverev to win the ATP Finals in Turin, becoming only the fourth player in history to hold all four Grand Slams and the ATP Finals title simultaneously. The others? Agassi, Federer, and Djokovic — an extraordinary club. At just 23 years old, Alcaraz is cementing himself as the defining tennis player of his generation. A great story for sport fans heading into the Australian Open season.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was ugly — the NASDAQ dropped 5.3% and the S&P 500 fell 3.7% in one of the worst single nights of the year. The ASX held up relatively well today, slipping just 0.26%. Gold surged 3.3% to a new high near $3,632 USD as investors fled to safety. Oil dipped slightly to $82.89.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Quiet session today — the ASX largely shrugged off the overnight US carnage, dropping only 0.26%.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw the S&P drop 3.7% — a significant one-day fall driven by broad selling across tech and growth stocks.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The NASDAQ cratered 5.28% last night — the tech-heavy index took the worst of the selloff, dragging down MSFT, GOOG and AI-related stocks.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Gold surged 3.3% to near $3,632 USD/oz last night — a classic 'fear trade' as investors fled stocks for safe-haven assets.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil slipped 1.3% to $82.89, despite the Middle East tanker incident. Watch this space — any escalation in the Gulf could reverse this quickly.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar was barely changed, sitting at 66.5 US cents. Relatively stable given the global market turbulence.

politics.summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers delivered a stark economic warning today — unemployment heading above 5%, inflation risks remaining, and a possible recession on the horizon. Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Penny Wong elevated AI as a national security issue, and Labor faces serious trouble in an upcoming Victorian by-election.

stories.title: Chalmers Warns of 'Triple-Whammy' — Unemployment, Inflation, and Possible Recession
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers used a major address today to warn Australians to brace for harder times ahead. He flagged that unemployment will surpass 5% (it's currently around 4.2%), inflation forecasts have worsened, and one closely-watched economic indicator suggests Australia could technically enter recession as early as next month. Chalmers found only 'modest' net savings in the budget and acknowledged it's 'no use pretending otherwise' — a rare moment of candour from a sitting Treasurer. This is significant for homeowners and mortgage holders as it complicates the RBA's path on interest rates.

stories.title: Australian Borrowers Face More Rate Hikes Before Relief in Late 2027
stories.why_it_matters: New analysis suggests Australian mortgage holders could face further interest rate increases before getting relief — with rate cuts not expected until late 2027 at the earliest. Combined with Chalmers' warning about rising unemployment, this paints a tough picture for anyone with a home loan. If you're on a variable rate, the pressure may not ease for another year or more.

stories.title: Penny Wong to Cast AI as a Major Foreign Policy and National Security Challenge
stories.why_it_matters: Foreign Minister Penny Wong is set to deliver a major speech framing AI as one of Australia's most pressing foreign policy challenges — not just an economic or tech issue. She's expected to argue that AI is reshaping global power dynamics, with authoritarian states using it for surveillance, disinformation, and military advantage. This signals the Albanese government is moving towards a more formal national security framework around AI, which could lead to new regulations or international agreements.

stories.title: Labor Faces 'Potentially Catastrophic' Result in Victorian By-Election
stories.why_it_matters: ABC News is reporting Labor faces a potentially catastrophic result in an upcoming Victorian by-election, with PM Albanese reportedly keeping his distance from the campaign. This follows a broader trend of federal Labor's support softening in Victoria. A bad result would add pressure on Albanese and could embolden internal critics — worth watching as a broader sign of the government's political health heading toward the next federal election.

stories.title: Gas Sector Called Out for 'Not Playing Fair' as Australia Pushes for More Supply
stories.why_it_matters: Australia is pushing for increased domestic gas supply to keep energy prices in check, but at least one major gas company is being called out for not honouring its domestic supply obligations. The government wants more gas flowing to Australian households and businesses rather than being exclusively exported. This is part of a broader energy affordability debate — gas prices are a key driver of power bills and manufacturing costs across the country.

ai.summary: AI governance is dominating the conversation this week — the Red Cross, US governors, American bishops, and a Washington Post opinion piece are all raising alarms about the pace of AI deployment outstripping regulation, particularly around autonomous weapons.

stories.title: Red Cross: 'Too Late Soon' to Regulate Autonomous Weapons
stories.why_it_matters: The International Red Cross has issued an urgent warning that the world is running out of time to regulate AI-powered autonomous weapons — drones and robots that can select and kill targets without a human making the final decision. The Red Cross says once these weapons are deployed at scale in active conflicts, it becomes almost impossible to ban them retroactively. Several nations are already testing autonomous weapons systems, and there is currently no binding international treaty restricting them. This isn't science fiction — it's happening now.

stories.title: US Governors Demand a Say in How AI is Regulated
stories.why_it_matters: A group of US state governors is pushing back against the idea that AI regulation should be purely a federal matter, arguing that states need their own powers to protect residents. This is a significant political fight — tech companies generally prefer one set of federal rules rather than 50 different state regulations. The outcome will shape how AI products are deployed across the US, which in turn affects the global AI industry and companies like Google and Microsoft that your portfolio holds.

stories.title: American Bishops Plan Mass Political Campaign for AI Regulation
stories.why_it_matters: The US Conference of Catholic Bishops is organising a 'groundswell' political campaign to push Congress to regulate artificial intelligence. The bishops are specifically concerned about AI being used to generate disinformation, exploit children, automate decisions about people's lives (like welfare or hiring), and create autonomous weapons. It's notable because religious institutions don't often wade into tech policy — this signals that AI regulation is becoming a mainstream political issue that crosses traditional left-right lines.

stories.title: Washington Post: America's AI Policy Has a 'Chip-Size Hole' in It
stories.why_it_matters: A Washington Post opinion piece argues that US AI policy has a critical gap: it focuses on software and models, but doesn't adequately control the semiconductor (computer chip) supply chain that makes advanced AI possible. The argument is that without controlling who gets access to the most powerful AI chips — particularly restricting China — any AI policy is incomplete. This matters for investors because chip restrictions directly affect companies like Nvidia, AMD, and by extension, the AI ETFs in your portfolio like GXAI.AX.

sport.summary: Carlos Alcaraz made history winning the ATP Finals, Jannik Sinner faces a nervous wait over his Australian Open participation, and the Roosters edged the Knights 19-18 in the NRL Grand Final.

stories.title: Roosters Pip Knights 19-18 in NRL Grand Final Thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters won the 2026 NRL Grand Final, beating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in a one-point classic at Accor Stadium last Sunday. It was about as close as it gets — a one-point margin in the biggest game of the year. The Roosters take home another premiership, continuing their status as one of the game's most successful clubs.

stories.title: Alcaraz Wins ATP Finals, Joins Agassi, Federer and Djokovic in Elite Club
stories.why_it_matters: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alexander Zverev in the ATP Finals final in Turin, becoming just the fourth man in history to hold all four Grand Slams and the ATP Finals simultaneously. The only others to achieve this are Andre Agassi, Roger Federer, and Novak Djokovic. At 23, Alcaraz is now firmly in the conversation as the greatest of his generation. It's a historic milestone as the tennis world heads into the Australian Open season.

stories.title: Jannik Sinner's Australian Open Participation in Doubt Due to Knee Injury
stories.why_it_matters: World No.1 Jannik Sinner is in doubt for the Australian Open after confirming a knee injury with three treatment options being evaluated — conservative management, an injection, or surgery. Sinner won the Australian Open in 2024 and 2025 and is the overwhelming favourite for the title. His absence would dramatically shake up the draw and open the door for Alcaraz — who just won the ATP Finals — to claim an Australian Open title.

stories.title: AFL Draft Wrap: Dons Sign 209cm Giant, Nine Players Get Rookie Lifelines
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL draft wrap reveals Essendon (the Dons) have signed a 209cm giant — an unusually tall key position player who will be one to watch as a development prospect. Nine players across various clubs also received rookie contract lifelines, keeping their AFL dreams alive. An ex-Kangaroos player also got an unlikely second chance at the top level. The AFL football carousel is in full swing ahead of the 2027 season.
